description: Publishing (C272, C273). Every change you make to an app (uploads, edit_file replaces, update_app settings, retheme…) and every change from the dashboard waits in the app's DRAFT: nobody sees it, not the users and not pre's testers. Nothing is ever published on its own: CALL "publish" WHEN A CHANGE IS COMPLETE (all its files together) AND ALWAYS BEFORE YOU FINISH YOUR TURN. The app's own settings (name, slug, publishing, bans, team, domains) are not in the draft: they change at once. Each app has a chosen environment, `target`: "pro" (the default: what the users have) or "pre" (a private copy the developer tests calmly, at the pre link, with its own data and Stripe's test mode). Actions: "status" — { target, draft: { count, files: [{ path, op: put|delete }], settings: [field], savedAt, dropped }, pre: what pre has that pro does not (only with target "pre") }; draft.dropped lists changes Neblla took out because they no longer fit its settings (a setting renamed or refused): tell the developer which. "publish" — the whole draft at once to the target. With target "pro" the users get it right now (returns { published, target, live: true, promotedAt, files, settings, message }): tell the developer "Publicado: ya se ve". With target "pre" only pre gets it (live: false). A publish costs no credits; with target "pro" it is one more version in "releases". A rooms change that discards data saved in pro needs confirmRoomsChange (error rooms_data_loss, nothing changed). "discard" — throw the draft away; the app stays as it was (confirm with the developer first). "to_pre" — «Pasar a pre»: from now on publishes go to pre only (for a redesign tried with the test card 4242 before the users see it). "promote" — «Subir a pro»: all of pre goes to pro at once and the target goes back to "pro" (with target "pro" it is the same as "publish"). "reset" — «Descartar» pre: pre goes back to what the users have and the target to "pro", without sending anything (confirm first). "diff" — what pre has that pro does not (files added/changed/removed, settings), plus `draft`. "releases" — the last versions the users had (Neblla keeps the last 10), newest first: { keep, releases: [{ id, at, by: { email, via: "dashboard"|"mcp" }, changes: { first, files: { added, changed, removed } each { count, paths }, settings: [field] }, files, rollbackOf, current }], queued }; an entry with id null is a release from before the history and cannot be sent again. "rollback" (releaseId) — send an earlier version back to pro, whole, at once (same answer as a publish to pro). The draft and pre are not touched. Confirm with the developer first; a rooms change that discards saved data needs confirmRoomsChange. In git, each environment is a branch (the developer's repo when linked with neblla_git, else Neblla's, see neblla_versions): when a version reaches pro, pre's branch is merged into pro's. The moderators follow the data, like the players: a pre on pro's data has pro's, a pre with its own data its own (neblla_set_moderator).

confirmRoomsChange.description: For "publish", "promote" and "rollback": accept a rooms change that discards data saved in pro
